name: Halcyon-Deep

civilization.name: The Thalassic Choirs
civilization.notes: Amphibious ocean-dwellers whose sunken cities still hum with dormant machinery; their fate remains unrecorded anywhere in settled space.

description: Halcyon-Deep hides beneath a dense shroud of vapor, a chill world of leaden seas broken by canyon walls that plunge five kilometers below the waves. The true ocean lies deeper still: beneath the crust, a subterranean sea wraps the entire planet, kept liquid by geothermal vent fields that burn like drowned constellations. Ice floes drift down from the poles even as steam rises from the canyon mouths.

Standing on a canyon rim, one hears the whole world breathing—a low resonant hum conducted through rock and water alike, rising and falling over hours. The dense air muffles everything else and presses on the eardrums like deep water. Visitors report vivid, shared dreams after a week on the surface, always of vast halls filled with singing.

The halls are real. The Thalassic Choirs built spiral cities down the canyon walls and into the crustal ocean itself, and their ruins remain impossibly preserved, lit here and there by machines still running after an unknown span of millennia. At the heart of the largest ruin stands a monolith of dark crystal that no scanner has ever penetrated, and it is from there that a signal rises through the planet's own hum—structured, patient, unanswered.

Every interstellar power wants what sleeps in Halcyon-Deep's ruins: the exotic matter alone would fund fleets. But landing parties come back changed in small ways, humming tunes no one taught them, and three survey ships have simply never left orbit. The signal has recently begun to change, shortening its intervals like something counting down. No one agrees on what happens when it reaches zero.
